result.description: Website builder and ecommerce platform; Commerce APIs expose orders, products, inventory, contacts, discounts, transactions and webhooks for merchant sites.
result.auth_detail: API key (Settings > Advanced > Developer API Keys) for a single merchant site's custom app, sent as a bearer token. OAuth2 auth-code for multi-site apps, but the client must first be registered with Squarespace and approved. Access tokens last 30 minutes. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
result.access_detail: To let other users connect, a developer must register an OAuth client and wait for Squarespace to review it and send back a client_id and client_secret. The API-key route needs no review, but it needs the paid Commerce Advanced plan and works on one site only. The Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth-only. Listing in Squarespace Extensions is a separate process.
result.api_notes: Commerce REST APIs: Analytics, Contacts, Discounts, Inventory, Orders, Products, Profiles (maintenance mode, replaced by Contacts), Transactions, Webhook Subscriptions. There is also a read-only Forms API (Zapier only) and a Websites entry. Page and content management is limited. The Orders API can import orders.
result.blocker: A public multi-tenant integration needs a Squarespace-reviewed OAuth client. The self-serve API-key path needs the paid Commerce Advanced plan and covers one site. The official MCP's Commerce tools are limited to Claude and ChatGPT.

evidence.quote: Depending on your development needs, you can use a generated API key or start the OAuth process with Squarespace to become a registered OAuth client.
With Squarespace's Commerce Advanced plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site.
We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible.
**Orders API:** Access order history for one-time purchases and subscription orders or import orders from third-party sales channels.
The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server. There's nothing to install.
